tooltip.refinedcooking:kitchen_station.d: Station node that connects to Refined Storage networks
jei.refinedcooking.kitchen_station.1: The Kitchen Station lets your Cooking for Blockheads cooking table craft with items — and fluids like water and milk — straight from your Refined Storage network.
jei.refinedcooking.kitchen_station.2: Place it in your kitchen beside the cooking table, or wired in through counters. Link it to a Kitchen Access Point on your network with a Kitchen Network Card; its screen lights up once connected.
The Kitchen Access Point sits on your Refined Storage network and projects it to a remote Kitchen Station. Open it and insert a Kitchen Network Card to choose which station to feed.

It reaches across distance and even dimensions, as long as both ends stay chunk-loaded. Its antennas light up while it is powered and active on the network, and it draws energy from the network like a Network Transmitter.
The Kitchen Network Card links the two blocks. Right-click a placed Kitchen Station to record its position, then insert the card into a Kitchen Access Point on your network to complete the link.
refinedcooking.guide.landing: Welcome!$(br2)$(2)Refined Cooking$() connects your $(6)Cooking for Blockheads$() kitchen with $(b)Refined Storage$(), letting you cook straight from your network inventory.
category.refinedcooking.name: Refined Cooking
category.refinedcooking.description: A mod that allows you to use items from your $(b)Refined Storage$() network inventory directly in your $(6)Cooking for Blockheads$() kitchen multi-block!$(br2)Two new blocks and one item are added to Minecraft.
entry.refinedcooking.kitchenstation.name: Kitchen Station
entry.refinedcooking.kitchenstation.intr: The $(l)Kitchen Station$() is the block that brings your $(b)Refined Storage$() network into the kitchen.$(br2)Placed in your $(6)Cooking for Blockheads$() kitchen, it hands the whole network inventory to the Cooking Table — every stored item becomes an ingredient. It even pulls $(o)fluids$() like water and milk from network storage.$(br2)A $(l)Kitchen Access Point$() reaches out and links it — from any distance, even another dimension.
entry.refinedcooking.kitchenstation.craf: Craft the $(l)Kitchen Station$() as shown.$(br2)Straight out of the grid it isn't tied to anything yet — a $(l)Kitchen Network Card$() and a $(l)Kitchen Access Point$() link it up. See those entries next.
entry.refinedcooking.kitchenstation.plac: An example kitchen layout — tap the eye to preview it in the world.
entry.refinedcooking.kitchenstation.stat: The Station's screen shows its status at a glance.$(br2)$(2)Lit$() means it's $(2)linked to a powered network$() — the Cooking Table can now cook with everything in your $(b)Refined Storage$() network, water and milk included.$(br2)$(4)Dark$() means it isn't connected. Check that a $(l)Kitchen Access Point$() holds a card pointing at it, that the network has power to spare, and that both ends stay chunk-loaded.
The $(l)Kitchen Access Point$() is the network end of the link.$(br2)It sits on your $(b)Refined Storage$() network and projects it out to a remote $(l)Kitchen Station$(). Open it and slot in a $(l)Kitchen Network Card$() to choose which Station it feeds — one Access Point serves one Station.$(br2)Like a $(b)Network Transmitter$(), it draws energy from the network while it runs.
Craft the $(l)Kitchen Access Point$() as shown.$(br2)Place it anywhere on your $(b)Refined Storage$() network — touching the Controller, a cable, or another machine.
An example network layout — tap the eye to preview it in the world.

The antennas and the card slot report two different things.$(br2)$(2)Lit antennas$() mean the Access Point is $(2)powered and active$() on the network. $(4)Dark$() means it's off the network, out of power, or switched off by redstone.$(br2)The $(l)card$() shows in its slot whenever one is inserted, independently of the antennas. A card sitting in a $(4)dark$() Access Point means the link is set up but nothing is running yet.
The $(l)Kitchen Network Card$() is what ties a $(l)Kitchen Station$() to a $(l)Kitchen Access Point$().$(br2)It remembers one Station's position and dimension — hover it in your inventory to see where it points.
Craft the $(l)Kitchen Network Card$() as shown.$(br2)One card links one Station to one Access Point.

$(l)1.$() Place the $(l)Kitchen Station$() in your kitchen.$(br)$(l)2.$() $(l)Right-click$() the Station with the card — it records that Station's position and dimension.$(br)$(l)3.$() Drop the card into a $(l)Kitchen Access Point$() on your powered network.$(br2)The Station lights up and the Cooking Table can reach your network — across any distance, even $(o)another dimension$(), as long as both ends stay chunk-loaded.$(br2)Take the card back out and the link drops.
